issues.issue: The definition operates entirely by reference to a blank form heading ("the person identified under the heading 'Customer' above"), which on this unexecuted form identifies no one.

The defined "we/us" is a single Texas entity, but the arbitration section (c073) expands "we" and "us" to affiliates and the opt-out notice (c094) is addressed to a different entity, PLS Financial Services.
The Lender is identified as a non-party, yet the arbitration and jury-waiver provisions (c052, c074) purport to bind and benefit "Lender" as though it were a contracting party.
The disclaimer of any lender or fiduciary role sits uneasily with the LOC and reimbursement obligations (c033–c038) under which CAB pays the lender and is repaid with 10% per annum interest.
The obligation is only to "attempt to" obtain a loan, issue the LOC and assist with documents, leaving the standard of performance for the fee undefined.
A one-day estimated performance period is hard to square with c008/c009, which describe reminder, education, check-cashing and branch-network services provided "throughout the term".

The listed additional services are hedged by "attempt to", "upon request", "where available" and "certain CAB services", so it is unclear what, if anything, is actually promised in return for the fee.
"The term" is not a defined period anywhere in this Agreement, and "may be provided" leaves it uncertain whether the additional services are promised at all.

"Denied by the Lender" is the only stated no-fee condition, while c021 says the CAB fee is "earned in advance at the inception of the loan"; the two must be harmonised for applications never acted on.
"Not open-ended in nature" is a conclusory characterisation with no operative content, and its meaning must be supplied from elsewhere.
The clause says the CAB fee "is not interest" yet must be included in the finance charge, an internal characterisation a party could argue cuts both ways on usury.
The rate is left as a garbled blank ("upon °% annualized rate"), so the central price term of the agreement is unstated on its face.
"Earned in advance at the inception of the loan" is in tension with c027, which entitles the customer to a prorated daily refund of part of the CAB fee on payment in full.
Every numeric term (loan amount, number of payments, Amount Financed, Finance Charge) is left blank and the sentence is truncated mid-phrase.
The amounts are blank and the text is garbled and truncated ("our CAB fee for this transaction ofS"), leaving the composition of the finance charge unstated.
The APR, payment dates, payment amounts and Total of Payments are all blank, so the payment schedule cannot be applied from the text.
The single payment-application waterfall covers late charges and returned item fees that c032 says are owed to the Lender rather than to CAB, leaving it unclear whose payments are being allocated.
"A refund of part of the CAB fee based on a prorated daily basis for the final period" does not say what "the final period" is or how the refund is computed.
The charge list ends with the open-ended "attorneys' fees, and costs of collection" appended to specific dollar items, leaving the reach of the catch-all uncertain.
The placement of "if payment is 10 or more days late" leaves it arguable whether the condition qualifies only the late charge or the whole list of lender charges.
The LOC is described as "irrevocable", yet c037 provides that it is "automatically revoked" on a timely cancellation and c036 fixes an expiry date.
The lender's bare statement of default suffices for payment even though c039 disclaims any duty to verify it, while c043 defines default by reference to the customer's own conduct.
Automatic revocation on cancellation cannot easily be squared with c033's statement that the LOC issued to the lender is "irrevocable" under Chapter 5 of the Texas Business and Commerce Code.

The disclaimer of responsibility for the accuracy of the lender's default statement sits against c034/c044, under which the customer is charged with reimbursing whatever CAB pays on that unverified statement.
The sentence is mangled ("unlgyuful excess", "reduced to the maximug peepee law"), so the savings mechanism it states cannot be read as written.
The sentence breaks off mid-word ("calculate charges by amortiz"), leaving the permitted method of computing charges incomplete.
Default limb (2), "if you fail to perform your other promises to us", is unbounded and could be triggered by any minor undertaking, including the certifications in c118–c120.
"We may exercise any other right or remedy allowed by law" is a catch-all appended to the single specific remedy of collecting a check, leaving its reach uncertain.

The right to "seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us" is in tension with c064, which forbids threatening or pursuing criminal charges related to a check given as security for a loan.
An anti-waiver clause preserving delayed enforcement bears on whether PLS could still demand arbitration after acting inconsistently with it (c074, c075), a point a court would have to reconcile.
"We are not required to file suit or arbitrate" is hard to reconcile with c071/c074, under which any Claim "shall be resolved by binding arbitration" upon either party's election.
The Agreement elsewhere refers only to a check or similar payment device and never grants a security interest, so "any collateral" has no referent in the instrument.
Permission to "sue or arbitrate with one or more persons without joining" others must be read against c106's flat prohibition on joinder or consolidation in any arbitration.
